result.title: SteerSearch: Interactive Search Reasoning with Mid-Response Steering
result.summary: Search-augmented language models increasingly serve as long-horizon research agents, yet most open training methods assume a fixed user goal throughout search. We study mid-response steering, where users redirect a model during ongoing reasoning or retrieval. We identify answer-target anchoring, a failure mode in which fixed-query search agents retrieve evidence for the updated request but still answer an earlier question. We introduce SteerSearch, an RL framework that trains on interactive search trajectories with injected interventions to enable context-preserving target reassignment, and SteerSearch-Bench, a benchmark adapted from multi-hop QA datasets. We also investigate Contrastive Context Reward (CCR), an auxiliary signal for aligning post-intervention reasoning with the updated goal. Without CCR, SteerSearch improves average steering accuracy over Search-R1 from 11.1% to 31.3% on Qwen2.5-3B and from 36.6% to 44.6% on Qwen3-4B, while preserving standard single-query performance. Gains also extend to larger Qwen2.5 models and natural multi-turn conversations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究检索增强语言模型在推理/检索过程中被用户中途改目标时的行为，指出「答案目标锚定」失败模式，提出 RL 框架 SteerSearch、配套基准 SteerSearch-Bench 以及 Contrastive Context Reward，以在保留上下文的前提下重新设定答案目标。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本搜索 agent 的中途目标重定向、上下文保持与「已检索新证据却仍回答旧问题」的失败诊断，可能为 LVR 中动态目标更新、检索证据是否真正被用于答案、以及推理轨迹的监督分配提供线索，可供核查。
